[LLM] GlobalProtect authentication from CVE-2026-0257 IOC IPs (Vultr / Dromatics) Delivery High
Detects GlobalProtect portal/gateway authentication events sourced from the Rapid7-published attacker IPs (Vultr 104.207.144.154 wave-1 and Dromatics 146.19.216.119/.120/.125 wave-2). Article-specific IP-watch for CVE-2026-0257 active exploitation. Rationale: IPs are explicitly enumerated as Rapid7 wave-1 (Vultr 104.207.144.154) and wave-2 (Dromatics 146.19.216.119/.120/.125) sources for CVE-2026-0257 cookie-forging exploitation, making any GlobalProtect connection from these addresses high-fidelity. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/pan-os-globalprotect-authentication.html

[LLM] GlobalProtect session with attacker-controlled machine names (GP-CLIENT / DESKTOP-GP01) Installation High
Surfaces GlobalProtect authentications where the client-reported machine name is GP-CLIENT (wave-1, May 17) or DESKTOP-GP01 (wave-2, May 21). These two hostnames are documented Rapid7 IOCs for CVE-2026-0257 cookie forgery. Rationale: GP-CLIENT and DESKTOP-GP01 are exact-string machine-name IOCs documented by Rapid7 for both CVE-2026-0257 exploitation waves; any GP session presenting them is high-confidence attacker activity. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/pan-os-globalprotect-authentication.html

[LLM] GlobalProtect VPN session with spoofed MAC aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff Delivery High
Detects GlobalProtect authentications reporting the all-purpose spoofed MAC address aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff. This MAC was reused across both Rapid7-observed CVE-2026-0257 exploitation waves and is a deterministic fingerprint of the threat actor's forged-cookie client. Rationale: aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff is the documented spoofed MAC reused across both Rapid7 waves; no legitimate endpoint should ever report this placeholder MAC, making it a near-zero-FP IOC for CVE-2026-0257 cookie forgery. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/pan-os-globalprotect-authentication.html
ATT&CKT1036 T1550.004

DeviceNetworkInfo | where Timestamp > ago(30d) | mv-expand MacAddress = MacAddress to typeof(string) | where tolower(MacAddress) == "aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff" or tolower(MacAddress) == "aabbccddeeff" | project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, NetworkAdapterName, MacAddress, IPAddresses | order by Timestamp desc
CommonSecurityLog | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where DeviceVendor has "Palo Alto" or DeviceProduct has_any ("GlobalProtect","PAN-OS") | where tolower(SourceMACAddress) in ("aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff","aabbccddeeff","aa-bb-cc-dd-ee-ff") or Message has "aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff" | project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, Activity, SourceIP, SourceUserName, SourceHostName, SourceMACAddress, DeviceAction, Message | order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Cookie-only GlobalProtect auth to local admin without preceding primary authentication Exploitation Medium
Hunts the CVE-2026-0257 exploitation primitive: GlobalProtect portal/gateway sessions established via authentication-override cookie to a local admin account when no primary authentication event preceded the cookie use within the lookback window. Targets the bearer-token replay behaviour Rapid7 attributes to the campaign. Rationale: Article specifically calls out "suspicious cookie-based authentication to local admin accounts" with no preceding primary auth as the CVE-2026-0257 signature; the anti-join against SigninLogs/SecurityEvent 4624/4768/4776 implements the missing-primary-auth pivot Rapid7 highlights. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/pan-os-globalprotect-authentication.html
ATT&CKT1212 T1539 T1550.004
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication
let CookieAuths = AlertEvidence | where Timestamp > ago(14d) | where AdditionalFields has_any ("globalprotect","authentication-override","GP-CLIENT","DESKTOP-GP01") | extend User = tolower(AccountName) | where User in ("admin","administrator","root","panadmin","gpadmin","localadmin") or User startswith "admin" | project Timestamp, User, RemoteIP, AccountUpn; CookieAuths | join kind=leftanti ( IdentityLogonEvents | where Timestamp > ago(14d) | where ActionType in ("LogonSuccess","LogonAttempted") | extend User = tolower(AccountName) | project PrimaryAuthTime = Timestamp, User ) on User | order by Timestamp desc
let lookback = 14d; let primary_window = 1h; let GpCookieAuths = CommonSecurityLog | where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback) | where DeviceVendor has "Palo Alto" or DeviceProduct has_any ("GlobalProtect","PAN-OS") | where Activity has_any ("authentication-override","cookie","auth-cookie","prelogin") or Message has_any ("authentication-override","auth-cookie") | extend User = tolower(coalesce(SourceUserName, DestinationHostName, AccountName)) | where User in ("admin","administrator","root","panadmin","gpadmin","localadmin") or User startswith "admin" | project CookieAuthTime = TimeGenerated, User, SourceIP, SourceHostName, SourceMACAddress, DeviceAction, Message; GpCookieAuths | join kind=leftanti ( union isfuzzy=true ( SigninLogs | where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback) | where ResultType == 0 | extend User = tolower(UserPrincipalName) | project PrimaryAuthTime = TimeGenerated, User ), ( SecurityEvent | where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback) | where EventID in (4624,4768,4776) | extend User = tolower(TargetUserName) | project PrimaryAuthTime = TimeGenerated, User ), ( CommonSecurityLog | where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback) | where DeviceVendor has "Palo Alto" | where Activity has_any ("ldap","radius","saml","local-user","login-success") and not (Activity has_any ("authentication-override","cookie")) | extend User = tolower(coalesce(SourceUserName, DestinationHostName, AccountName)) | project PrimaryAuthTime = TimeGenerated, User ) ) on User | order by CookieAuthTime desc
source:(paloalto OR pan_os OR globalprotect) (@evt.name:(authentication-override OR auth-cookie OR "cookie authentication") OR @action:authentication-override) @usr.name:(admin OR administrator OR root OR panadmin OR gpadmin OR localadmin)

Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-0257")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-0257")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-0257")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-0257")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.

Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("104.207.144.154", "146.19.216.119", "146.19.216.120", "146.19.216.125") or RemoteUrl has_any ("")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic(["104.207.144.154", "146.19.216.119", "146.19.216.120", "146.19.216.125"]);
let BadDomains = dynamic([""]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)

GREYVIBE Hackers Leverage ChatGPT and Google Gemini to Fuel Cyberattacks

Cyber Security News
2026-05-30 16 use cases 9 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

GREYVIBE hackers are increasingly leveraging generative AI tools such as ChatGPT and Google Gemini to enhance cyberattack operations. The campaign, active since at least August 2025, primarily targets Ukraine and related entities across the government, military, and civilian sectors, highlighting a growing convergence between artificial intelligence and modern cyber warfare. WithSecure researchers identified GREYVIBE as [&#8230;] The post GREYVIBE Hackers Leverage ChatGPT and Google Gemini to Fuel Cyberattacks appeared first on Cyber Security News .

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] GREYVIBE fake-CAPTCHA ClickFix: browser/Run-dialog -> PowerShell with paste-execute payload · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] GREYVIBE sample hashes (PhantomRelay/LegionRelay/DAYLIGHT/TEASOUP) on disk or executed · Scheduled task created with suspicious image / encoded args · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] GREYVIBE C2 egress: connections to PhantomRelay/LegionRelay infrastructure · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] LegionRelay/PhantomRelay PowerShell RAT collection: Telegram/WhatsApp/browser credential access · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
[LLM] GREYVIBE C2 egress: connections to PhantomRelay/LegionRelay infrastructure Command & Control High
Hunts outbound network and DNS activity to the eight GREYVIBE C2 IPs and eight domains (princess-mens*, strip-mens, zoomconference.click/app, frontforce.org, lapas.live) tied to the PrincessClub/adult-club lure and Ukrainian-government impersonation campaigns. This is the foundational IOC pivot and surfaces any host that has reached the threat group's infrastructure regardless of which stage (DAYLIGHT loader, PhantomRelay, LegionRelay) was used. Rationale: All 16 IOCs are taken verbatim from the article's pre-extracted block and corroborated by the WithSecure Labs GREYVIBE write-up and BleepingComputer's reporting. The princess-mens / strip-mens domains are the PrincessClub adult-club lure infrastructure WithSecure tied to LegionRelay/PhantomRelay delivery; the 89.125.189.x and 194.87.x ranges are dedicated GREYVIBE hosters, so even a single hit is high-fidelity. Cross-checked against: • https://labs.withsecure.com/publications/greyvibe • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/greyvibe-hackers-use-chatgpt-gemini-to-power-cyberattacks/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/new-russian-linked-greyvibe-targets.html
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071 T1583.001

[LLM] GREYVIBE sample hashes (PhantomRelay/LegionRelay/DAYLIGHT/TEASOUP) on disk or executed Installation High
Direct SHA256 match against the eight WithSecure-published GREYVIBE samples covering DAYLIGHT loader, TEASOUP obfuscator, PhantomRelay PowerShell RAT, and LegionRelay. Hits across DeviceProcessEvents (executed) and DeviceFileEvents (written/dropped) so we catch both detonation and staging. Rationale: Eight SHA256s come straight from the article's pre-extracted IOCs and are corroborated against the WithSecure GREYVIBE technical write-up. Hash matches on running process or on-disk drop are the highest-fidelity signal possible — zero plausible benign collisions on SHA256. Cross-checked against: • https://labs.withsecure.com/publications/greyvibe • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/greyvibe-hackers-use-chatgpt-gemini-to-power-cyberattacks/

[LLM] GREYVIBE fake-CAPTCHA ClickFix: browser/Run-dialog -> PowerShell with paste-execute payload Delivery High
Hunts the specific GREYVIBE delivery technique: a Ukrainian-language fake CAPTCHA page tricks the victim into pasting and executing a PowerShell/cmd command via Win+R or paste-to-terminal as a 'verification step'. Process tree shows explorer.exe or a browser as the parent of powershell/cmd/mshta with download or base64 payload, often referencing one of the GREYVIBE domains. Rationale: WithSecure's write-up and the article both call out the fake-CAPTCHA flow with Ukrainian-language verification steps as the PrincessClub lure's primary delivery. Parent-of-shell being explorer.exe (Win+R) or a browser, plus paste-execute keywords (iex/DownloadString/-EncodedCommand) AND/OR explicit GREYVIBE domain references, gives a clean signal that distinguishes this from generic LOLBaS noise. Cross-checked against: • https://labs.withsecure.com/publications/greyvibe • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/greyvibe-hackers-use-chatgpt-gemini-to-power-cyberattacks/
ATT&CKT1204.004 T1059.001 T1059.003 T1566.002

DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("explorer.exe","chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (SuspectCmd)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
let SuspectCmd = dynamic(["iex","invoke-expression","downloadstring","invoke-webrequest","iwr ","frombase64string","webclient","-encodedcommand","-enc ","-ec ","certutil -urlcache","curl ","bitsadmin","captcha","verification","verify","cloudflare","frontforce.org","lapas.live","zoomconference.click","zoomconference.app","princess-mens","strip-mens"]);

  (ImProcessCreate
     | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
     | where ParentProcessName has_any ("explorer.exe","chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
     | where ActingProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe")
     | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (SuspectCmd)
     | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine),

title: GREYVIBE Fake-CAPTCHA ClickFix - Browser/Explorer Spawns Shell With Paste-Execute Payload
id: 5d9c2a8e-6b4f-49c7-a3f1-8e2d6b9c4f1a
description: Browser or Win+R Run-dialog (explorer.exe) spawning powershell.exe / cmd.exe / mshta.exe with a command line that contains paste-execute markers (iex, DownloadString, -EncodedCommand) or references to GREYVIBE lure infrastructure (princess-mens, strip-mens, zoomconference.click). This is the ClickFix delivery vector WithSecure reports for the PrincessClub adult-club campaign.
references:
  - https://labs.withsecure.com/publications/greyvibe
  - https://cybersecuritynews.com/greyvibe-hackers-chatgpt-and-google-gemini/

      - '\opera.exe'
  selection_child:

      - '\cmd.exe'

      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'

      - 'Invoke-Expression'

      - 'Invoke-WebRequest'
      - 'FromBase64String'
      - '-EncodedCommand'
      - 'WebClient'

      - 'lapas.live'

[LLM] LegionRelay/PhantomRelay PowerShell RAT collection: Telegram/WhatsApp/browser credential access Actions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the LegionRelay/PhantomRelay post-compromise collection pattern WithSecure documents: a PowerShell process touching Telegram Desktop tdata, WhatsApp Local State, and/or Chromium-family Login Data / Cookies / Local State within a tight window — the unique fingerprint of LegionRelay's file-theft and credential-exfil routines. Rationale: WithSecure explicitly states LegionRelay supports 'file theft, screenshot capturing, browser credential theft, Telegram and WhatsApp data exfiltration' and that PhantomRelay is PowerShell-based. PowerShell touching ≥3 distinct browser-credential or messenger-data paths within 15 minutes is the structural fingerprint of that collection routine. Skipped Sigma because the detection requires distinct-count aggregation across multiple file events, which Sigma's single-event-selection model does not express cleanly. Cross-checked against: • https://labs.withsecure.com/publications/greyvibe • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/greyvibe-hackers-use-chatgpt-gemini-to-power-cyberattacks/

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files

LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName

// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

            - '\MsSense.exe'
            - '\MsMpEng.exe'
            - '\csrss.exe'
            - '\svchost.exe'
            - '\wininit.exe'
            - '\services.exe'
            - '\lsm.exe'
            - '\SearchProtocolHost.exe'
    condition: selection and not filter_known_good
falsepositives:
    - Third-party EDR / forensic tools — extend the filter list
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1021.002
    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_psexec:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'
            - '\smbexec.py'
    selection_wmic_remote:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\wmic.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/node:'
    condition: selection_psexec or selection_wmic_remote
falsepositives:
    - Sysadmins running approved remote-management tooling — wrap with
      a known-admin-host watchlist
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard Installation High
ConnectWise / AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera installed outside IT change windows = common tradecraft for ransomware affiliates and IT-helpdesk impersonators.
ATT&CKT1219
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe")
   or FileName matches regex @"(?i)kaseya.*\.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\AnyDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer_Service.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\atera_agent.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\SplashtopStreamer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\RustDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\NinjaOne.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Critical

Malicious npm packages abuse dependency confusion to profile developer environments

Microsoft Security Blog
2026-05-30 16 use cases 6 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

A dependency confusion campaign leveraged 33 malicious npm packages to collect reconnaissance data from developer and build environments. This report details the attack chain, observed tradecraft, and detection opportunities to help organizations identify and disrupt related activity. The post Malicious npm packages abuse dependency confusion to profile developer environments appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog .

ATT&CKT1027 T1195.002 T1204.002 T1219 T1486 T1566
Domainsoob.moika.tech moika.tech cloudplatform-single-spa.io github.cloudplatform-single-spa.io docs.cloudplatform-single-spa.io jira.cloudplatform-single-spa.io telemetry.cloudplatform-single-spa.io t-in-one.io npm.t-in-one.io docs.t-in-one.io

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] npm install of dependency-confusion scoped packages (moika.tech actor) · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Malicious npm packages abuse dependency confusion to profile developer environme
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Malicious postinstall.js dropped under node_modules for actor scopes · [LLM] node.exe spawns detached child from tmpdir after npm install (moika.tech dropper) · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] C2 callback to moika.tech payload distribution infrastructure · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft)
[LLM] npm install of dependency-confusion scoped packages (moika.tech actor) Delivery High
Detects npm/node executing install lifecycle hooks for any of the nine attacker-controlled organizational scopes published by mr.4nd3r50n, ce-rwb, and t-in-one on 2026-05-28/29. The scope strings appear in the resolution command line during npm install, making this a high-fidelity early-stage signal. Rationale: Anchored on the nine attacker-controlled npm scopes named in the article (@cloudplatform-single-spa, @wb-track, @data-science, @ce-rwb, @payments-widget, @travel-autotests, @t-in-one, @capibar.chat, @sber-ecom-core) — these are not real internal namespaces, so any developer-host hit is by definition an unwanted install.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where FileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe","npx.cmd","npx.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe","npx.cmd","npx.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (
    "@cloudplatform-single-spa","@wb-track","@data-science/",
    "@ce-rwb","@payments-widget","@travel-autotests",
    "@t-in-one","@capibar.chat","@sber-ecom-core")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (
    "@cloudplatform-single-spa","@wb-track","@data-science/",
    "@ce-rwb","@payments-widget","@travel-autotests",
    "@t-in-one","@capibar.chat","@sber-ecom-core")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\node.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "\\npm.cmd" or NewProcessName endswith "\\npm.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "\\npx.cmd" or ParentProcessName endswith "\\node.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "\\npm.cmd"
| where CommandLine has_any (
    "@cloudplatform-single-spa","@wb-track","@data-science/",
    "@ce-rwb","@payments-widget","@travel-autotests",
    "@t-in-one","@capibar.chat","@sber-ecom-core")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, ParentProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: npm Install of Moika.tech Dependency-Confusion Scoped Packages
id: 5b3d9a26-1c8e-4b9f-9b1c-2e7e0c5a3f12
description: Detects npm/node executing install for malicious scoped packages published by the mr.4nd3r50n / ce-rwb / t-in-one cluster (Microsoft Threat Intelligence, 2026-05-29).
references:
  - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/05/29/33-malicious-npm-packages-abuse-dependency-confusion-profile-developer-environments/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/30
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.007
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\node.exe'
      - '\npm.cmd'
      - '\npm.exe'
      - '\npx.cmd'
      - '\npx.exe'
  selection_scope:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '@cloudplatform-single-spa'
      - '@wb-track'
      - '@data-science/'
      - '@ce-rwb'
      - '@payments-widget'
      - '@travel-autotests'
      - '@t-in-one'
      - '@capibar.chat'
      - '@sber-ecom-core'
  condition: selection_proc and selection_scope
level: high
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.security) (@EventID:1 OR @EventID:4688) (@Image:(*\\node.exe OR *\\NODE.EXE OR *\\npm.cmd OR *\\NPM.CMD OR *\\npm.exe OR *\\npx.cmd OR *\\npx.exe) OR @ParentImage:(*\\node.exe OR *\\npm.cmd OR *\\npm.exe)) @CommandLine:(*@cloudplatform-single-spa* OR *@wb-track* OR *@data-science/* OR *@ce-rwb* OR *@payments-widget* OR *@travel-autotests* OR *@t-in-one* OR *@capibar.chat* OR *@sber-ecom-core*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\\(node|npm|npx)(\.exe|\.cmd)?$/i OR ParentBaseFileName=/^(node|npm|npx)(\.exe|\.cmd)?$/i
| regex("@(cloudplatform-single-spa|wb-track|data-science/|ce-rwb|payments-widget|travel-autotests|t-in-one|capibar\.chat|sber-ecom-core)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe","npx.cmd","npx.exe") OR Processes.parent_process_name IN ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe","npx.cmd","npx.exe")) AND (Processes.process="*@cloudplatform-single-spa*" OR Processes.process="*@wb-track*" OR Processes.process="*@data-science/*" OR Processes.process="*@ce-rwb*" OR Processes.process="*@payments-widget*" OR Processes.process="*@travel-autotests*" OR Processes.process="*@t-in-one*" OR Processes.process="*@capibar.chat*" OR Processes.process="*@sber-ecom-core*" OR Processes.parent_process="*@cloudplatform-single-spa*" OR Processes.parent_process="*@wb-track*" OR Processes.parent_process="*@t-in-one*" OR Processes.parent_process="*@capibar.chat*" OR Processes.parent_process="*@sber-ecom-core*") by _time Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe","npx.cmd","npx.exe") OR Processes.parent_process_name IN ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe","npx.cmd","npx.exe")) AND (Processes.process="*@cloudplatform-single-spa*" OR Processes.process="*@wb-track*" OR Processes.process="*@data-science/*" OR Processes.process="*@ce-rwb*" OR Processes.process="*@payments-widget*" OR Processes.process="*@travel-autotests*" OR Processes.process="*@t-in-one*" OR Processes.process="*@capibar.chat*" OR Processes.process="*@sber-ecom-core*" OR Processes.parent_process="*@cloudplatform-single-spa*" OR Processes.parent_process="*@wb-track*" OR Processes.parent_process="*@t-in-one*" OR Processes.parent_process="*@capibar.chat*" OR Processes.parent_process="*@sber-ecom-core*") by _time Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
[LLM] C2 callback to moika.tech payload distribution infrastructure Command & Control High
Detects outbound HTTPS from any process to oob.moika.tech or the parent moika.tech domain — the dropper fetches its platform-specific payload from https://oob.moika.tech/payload/{win|mac|linux}. Catches the post-install reconnaissance stager regardless of which scope triggered it. Rationale: oob.moika.tech (and the parent moika.tech) is the single C2 endpoint named in the article — every package in the cluster fetches https://oob.moika.tech/payload/<platform>. Domain has no legitimate dev-tooling use and was first seen in this campaign on 2026-05-28.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("oob.moika.tech","moika.tech")
   or RemoteUrl matches regex @"(?i)moika\.tech/payload/(win|mac|linux)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
  (CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where DestinationHostName has_any ("oob.moika.tech","moika.tech")
         or RequestURL has_any ("oob.moika.tech","moika.tech/payload/")
    | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourceHostName, DestinationHostName, DestinationIP, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication, DeviceVendor),
  (DnsEvents
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where Name has "moika.tech"
    | project TimeGenerated, ClientIP, Computer, Name, QueryType, Result, ServerIPAddress),
  (ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where HttpHostName has_any ("oob.moika.tech","moika.tech") or Url has "moika.tech/payload/"
    | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, HttpHostName, Url, HttpMethod, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

      - 'moika.tech'

level: high

(#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/moika\.tech$/i) OR (#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 ContextImageFileName=/\\(node|npm|npx)(\.exe|\.cmd)?$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName, RemoteAddressIP4], function=count())

[LLM] Malicious postinstall.js dropped under node_modules for actor scopes Installation High
Detects the obfuscated ~7 KB postinstall.js stager being materialised inside node_modules/@<actor-scope>/<pkg>/scripts/postinstall.js. Hunting tier because file-event volume from npm installs is high — the value is in retrospective hunts and forensic timeline reconstruction. Rationale: The article specifies `scripts/postinstall.js` as the obfuscated stager, dropped under each malicious scoped package. Pairing the literal filename with the actor's nine scope strings inside node_modules yields a near-zero-FP file event because no legitimate package would publish under these namespaces.

[LLM] node.exe spawns detached child from tmpdir after npm install (moika.tech dropper) Installation Medium
After fetching the platform payload, the obfuscated stager writes it to the OS tmpdir and spawns a detached child. Detects node.exe spawning a process whose image lives in %TEMP% / %TMP% / /tmp where the grandparent chain involves npm — catches stage-2 even if the C2 domain rotates. Rationale: Article describes the deobfuscated execution flow: stager fetches payload from oob.moika.tech, writes it to tmpdir, then spawns a detached child. Constraining node.exe parent + tmpdir child path + correlation with a recent npm install on the same host turns a noisy primitive (node spawning anything) into a campaign-specific signal.
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1105 T1564.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
let NpmHosts = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where FileName in~ ("npm.cmd","npm.exe","npx.cmd")
        or ProcessCommandLine has "npm install"
    | project DeviceId, NpmTime = Timestamp;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node.exe"
| where FolderPath has_any (
    @"\AppData\Local\Temp\",
    @"\Windows\Temp\",
    "/tmp/",
    "/var/folders/")
| where FileName !in~ ("conhost.exe","node.exe")
| join kind=inner NpmHosts on DeviceId
| where Timestamp between (NpmTime .. NpmTime + 30m)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName,

| order by Timestamp desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT

| tstats `summariesonly` count

    [| tstats `summariesonly` count

          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count

    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user

    [| tstats summariesonly=false count

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files

LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents

| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,

| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] praisonai-platform CVE-2026-47416: PATCH /workspaces/{id}/members/{user_id} role-change request Exploitation High
Hunts the core privilege-escalation primitive in CVE-2026-47416 — an HTTP PATCH against /workspaces/<workspace_id>/members/<user_id> on praisonai-platform <=0.1.2. Because require_workspace_member defaults to min_role='member' and the route never overrides it, any authenticated member can write {"role":"owner"} to any member row. Outside of one-off legitimate owner-driven role tweaks this URL+verb pair is extremely rare, so even URI-only telemetry is high-fidelity for affected deployments. Rationale: Article pinpoints the exact endpoint shape (PATCH /workspaces/{workspace_id}/members/{user_id}) and the route file (api/routes/workspaces.py:115-127). Even without request-body visibility, the verb+path pair is rare enough on praisonai-platform to be high-fidelity; restricting on HTTP 2xx removes 401/403 noise from unaffected versions. Cross-checked against the GHSA advisory body and corroborated by independent PraisonAI security coverage on cybersecuritynews.com and Sysdig confirming the platform's pattern of weakly-gated workspace endpoints. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-c2m8-4gcg-v22g • https://cybersecuritynews.com/praisonai-vulnerability-exploited/ • https://www.sysdig.com/blog/cve-2026-44338-praisonai-authentication-bypass-in-under-4-hours-and-the-growing-trend-of-rapid-exploitation
ATT&CKT1068 T1190 T1098

title: praisonai-platform CVE-2026-47416 PATCH workspaces members role-change
id: 7a4cbf8e-2b39-4b9a-a4ba-2026474160c1
status: experimental
description: Detects HTTP PATCH requests against the praisonai-platform /workspaces/{workspace_id}/members/{user_id} endpoint that exposes a vertical privilege-escalation primitive (CVE-2026-47416). The endpoint should normally see near-zero PATCH traffic; any successful PATCH is suspicious until the deployment is patched to >=0.1.3 with the min_role='owner' gate applied.
references:

author: SOC Detection Engineering

[LLM] praisonai-platform CVE-2026-47416: Member self-promotion + legitimate-owner demotion chain within one hour Installation High
Catches the two-request takeover chain described in the advisory — the attacker first self-promotes (PATCH on their own user_id with {"role":"owner"}) and then demotes the legitimate owner (PATCH on the owner's user_id with {"role":"member"}). This temporal pivot is much higher fidelity than UC1 because legitimate workspace operations almost never produce two role-mutating PATCHs from the same client IP within a short window. Rationale: The advisory explicitly calls out the two-PATCH primitive: 'owner lockout in two requests total'. Workspaces where the same client IP/user mutates 2+ distinct member rows within the hour is a behaviour the legitimate UI essentially never produces — owners normally change one role at a time and rarely demote themselves seconds after promoting. Threshold of >=2 distinct TargetUser within 60m is the article's own attack cadence. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-c2m8-4gcg-v22g
ATT&CKT1098 T1531 T1136.003
Data sourcesWeb.Web
let Lookback = 7d;
let WindowMin = 60m;
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
| where HttpMethod =~ "PATCH"
| where Url matches regex @"(?i)/workspaces/[^/]+/members/[^/?#]+"
| where HttpStatusCode in ("200","204")
| extend Workspace = extract(@"(?i)/workspaces/([^/]+)/members/", 1, Url)
| extend TargetUser = extract(@"(?i)/workspaces/[^/]+/members/([^/?#]+)", 1, Url)
| summarize PatchCount = count(),
            TargetsTouched = dcount(TargetUser),
            Targets = make_set(TargetUser, 10),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
            by SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, Workspace, bin(TimeGenerated, WindowMin)
| where PatchCount >= 2 and TargetsTouched >= 2   // self-promote + owner-demote = 2 distinct user_ids
| extend WindowMinutes = datetime_diff('minute', LastSeen, FirstSeen)
| order by FirstSeen desc

[LLM] praisonai-platform CVE-2026-47416: Bulk agent/issue/project/comment enumeration immediately after a workspace role-change PATCH Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects the collection phase of the takeover chain — once the attacker holds owner via the CVE-2026-47416 primitive they pivot into LIST endpoints (agents, issues, projects, comments) that were previously gated by owner-tier access. The detection joins a successful PATCH on /workspaces/*/members/* with a burst of GET/LIST traffic from the same session within 15 minutes, flagging the post-elevation data harvest. Rationale: Article explicitly chains the elevation into 'exfiltrate everything via the agent/issue/project/comment IDORs that were filed as separate advisories'. The named LIST endpoints come from the advisory's own corroboration section. Pairing the elevation event with the post-elevation enumeration inside 15 minutes weeds out generic browse traffic from a non-attack owner. Burst threshold of 10 distinct GETs is calibrated to the article's described mass-pull behaviour rather than a casual single-resource read. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-c2m8-4gcg-v22g
ATT&CKT1213 T1530 T1087.004
Data sourcesWeb.Web
let Lookback = 7d;
let PostWindow = 15m;
let BurstThreshold = 10;   // 10+ list calls inside 15m post-PATCH = harvest-shaped
let RoleChanges = ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
    | where HttpMethod =~ "PATCH"
    | where Url matches regex @"(?i)/workspaces/[^/]+/members/[^/?#]+"
    | where HttpStatusCode in ("200","204")
    | project PatchTime = TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, PatchedWorkspace = extract(@"(?i)/workspaces/([^/]+)/members/", 1, Url);
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
| where HttpMethod =~ "GET"
| where Url matches regex @"(?i)/workspaces/[^/]+/(agents|issues|projects|comments)"
| join kind=inner RoleChanges on SrcIpAddr
| where TimeGenerated between (PatchTime .. PatchTime + PostWindow)
| summarize ListCount = count(),
            DistinctResources = dcount(extract(@"(?i)/workspaces/[^/]+/(agents|issues|projects|comments)", 1, Url)),
            ListUrls = make_set(Url, 25),
            FirstList = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastList = max(TimeGenerated)
            by SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, PatchedWorkspace, PatchTime
| where ListCount >= BurstThreshold
| extend DelaySeconds = datetime_diff('second', FirstList, PatchTime)
| order by PatchTime desc

[LLM] Vulnerable praisonai-platform deployment hunt (uvicorn launching praisonai_platform.api.app) Installation High
Surfaces hosts running praisonai-platform — the vulnerable component in CVE-2026-47410. Defaults bypass the secret-guard when PLATFORM_ENV is unset (its default is 'dev'), so any deployment started without explicitly exporting PLATFORM_JWT_SECRET is exploitable. This UC identifies the population that needs urgent remediation before attackers find them on Shodan. Rationale: Pivots on the exact startup invocation named in the advisory (`uvicorn praisonai_platform.api.app:app`) and the package import name. The `--reload` exclusion drops developer workstations where the dev server is intentional. The SecretInCmdLine/ProdEnvInCmdLine extends help the analyst decide remediation urgency at triage time without a second query.
ATT&CKT1190 T1552.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has "uvicorn"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("praisonai_platform.api.app", "praisonai_platform", "praisonai-platform")
| where not(ProcessCommandLine has "--reload")              // dev-mode flag, common on developer workstations
| extend SecretInCmdLine = ProcessCommandLine has "PLATFORM_JWT_SECRET"
| extend ProdEnvInCmdLine = ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)PLATFORM_ENV\s*=\s*(prod|production|stage|staging)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          SecretInCmdLine, ProdEnvInCmdLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent

| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] praisonai-platform cross-tenant workspace operations from single source IP Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects JWT-forgery exploitation against CVE-2026-47410. After minting a token with arbitrary 'sub', the attacker hits authenticated routes — /auth/me to validate, then POST /workspaces/{id}/members, PATCH /workspaces/{id}, or DELETE /workspaces/{id} across multiple distinct workspace UUIDs. Catches the post-forgery pivot where one IP authenticates as many different user_ids in a short window — a pattern legitimate users do not produce. Rationale: Anchors on the exact route shapes the advisory's exploit chain calls out (steps 5-6: /auth/me + cross-workspace POST/PATCH/DELETE). The 'distinct workspaces >= 3 within 30m from one source IP' threshold captures the asymmetry between a legitimate user (their own 1-2 workspaces) and a forger pivoting across tenants. Falcon LogScale and CloudWatch left empty because FDR doesn't ship app-tier HTTP request logs and the CloudTrail/VPC schema doesn't carry the request path; this detection genuinely needs reverse-proxy/WAF telemetry the host SIEM aggregates.
ATT&CKT1078 T1190 T1212
Data sourcesWeb.Web
// Best-effort proxy via inbound network telemetry — true detection lives in web logs (see sentinel_kql).
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(24h)
| where ActionType == "InboundConnectionAccepted"
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("praisonai_platform", "praisonai-platform") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "uvicorn"
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| summarize InboundCount = count(), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), DistinctPorts = dcount(LocalPort)
   by DeviceName, RemoteIP, InitiatingProcessFileName
| where InboundCount > 50
| order by InboundCount desc
let WindowMinutes = 30m;
let WorkspaceRegex = @"/workspaces/([0-9a-f\-]{8,})";
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where RequestURL has_any ("/auth/me", "/auth/register", "/workspaces/")
| extend Method = toupper(coalesce(RequestMethod, DeviceCustomString1))
| extend WorkspaceId = extract(WorkspaceRegex, 1, RequestURL)
| extend IsDestructive = Method in ("DELETE", "PATCH") or (Method == "POST" and RequestURL has "/members")
| extend IsAuthMe = RequestURL has "/auth/me"
| extend IsRegister = RequestURL has "/auth/register"
| summarize
    AuthMeHits = countif(IsAuthMe),
    RegisterHits = countif(IsRegister),
    DistinctWorkspaces = dcountif(WorkspaceId, isnotempty(WorkspaceId)),
    DestructiveOps = countif(IsDestructive),
    SampleWorkspaces = make_set_if(WorkspaceId, isnotempty(WorkspaceId), 10),
    SampleURLs = make_set(RequestURL, 15),
    Methods = make_set(Method, 10),
    FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
    LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
    by SourceIP, bin(TimeGenerated, WindowMinutes)
| where DistinctWorkspaces >= 3 and DestructiveOps >= 1   // 3 = empirical: a real user touches their own 1-2 workspaces; cross-tenant pivot starts at 3+
| order by LastSeen desc
@http.url_details.path:("/auth/me" OR *"/workspaces/"* OR "/auth/register") @http.method:(DELETE OR PATCH OR POST) -@http.useragent:(*HealthCheck* OR *k6* OR *Locust* OR *Prometheus*)

| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web.Web where (Web.url="*/auth/me*" OR Web.url="*/workspaces/*" OR Web.url="*/auth/register*") by Web.src Web.url Web.http_method Web.user _time span=30m | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | rex field=url "/workspaces/(?<workspace_id>[0-9a-f\-]{8,})" | eval destructive=if(match(http_method,"(?i)DELETE|PATCH|POST") AND match(url,"/workspaces/"),1,0) | stats dc(workspace_id) as distinct_workspaces dc(user) as distinct_users sum(destructive) as destructive_ops values(http_method) as methods values(url) as urls min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime by src | where distinct_workspaces >= 3 AND destructive_ops >= 1 | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - lastTime
