Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process Exploitation High
Classic macro/exploit pattern — Office app launching cmd/powershell/wmic/regsvr32.

DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)

| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\winword.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\excel.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\powerpnt.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\outlook.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\onenote.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\mspub.exe"

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d07
status: experimental
description: |
    Word/Excel/Outlook/OneNote spawning powershell, cmd, wscript,
    cscript, mshta, rundll32, regsvr32 — classic macro / embedded-
    object payload signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059
    - attack.t1566.001
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\winword.exe'
            - '\excel.exe'
            - '\powerpnt.exe'
            - '\outlook.exe'
            - '\onenote.exe'
            - '\mspub.exe'
            - '\visio.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate automation macros in trusted internal documents
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) Exploitation High
Browser-pasted PowerShell launched from explorer/Run dialog — ClickFix social engineering.
ATT&CKT1204.004 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\explorer.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\RuntimeBroker.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/

date: 2026/05/02
tags:

    - attack.initial-access

            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'

[LLM] vm2 vulnerable version inventory (CVE-2026-47140) — NodeVM denylist bypass surface Weaponization High
Surfaces hosts running npm:vm2 <= 3.11.3 which is vulnerable to the NodeVM builtin denylist bypass via the `process` and `inspector/promises` modules. Pre-incident asset hygiene UC to identify exposed Node.js services before exploitation. Rationale: Article names the affected package and version range (npm:vm2 <= 3.11.3) and the CVE ID directly. Cross-checked with The Hacker News reporting and Heise that the fix lands in vm2 3.11.4 alongside three sibling criticals (CVE-2026-47208/47137/47131). Internet-facing weighting added because vm2 is most dangerous when fronting an attacker-supplied JS-eval endpoint. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/vm2-nodejs-library-vulnerabilities.html • https://www.heise.de/en/news/Node-js-Four-critical-security-gaps-with-maximum-rating-in-vm2-closed-11300471.html • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rp36-8xq3-r6c4

[LLM] Node.js process spawning native shell / interpreter — post-vm2-escape host execution Exploitation Medium
Detects `node.exe` (or `node` on Linux) spawning a native shell or Windows LOLBin as a child process. After the CVE-2026-47140 escape, the attacker reaches `child_process.execFileSync(...)` in the host Node.js process — every successful exploitation surfaces here as an unexpected node→shell parent/child edge. Rationale: Article's PoC is `require("process").getBuiltinModule("child_process").execFileSync(...)` — every successful sandbox escape walks through node.exe → spawned-binary. Cross-checked with Hacker News and Semgrep coverage of the four sibling vm2 CVEs (47208/47137/47140/47131) confirming this parent/child edge is the common post-exploit primitive. The npm/yarn/pnpm filter strips the dominant FP class (lifecycle scripts). Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/vm2-nodejs-library-vulnerabilities.html • https://semgrep.dev/blog/2026/calling-back-to-vm2-and-escaping-sandbox/ • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rp36-8xq3-r6c4

description: Detects node.exe spawning a Windows shell or LOLBin — the post-exploitation surface of vm2 NodeVM sandbox-escape CVEs (CVE-2026-47140 / 47208 / 47137 / 47131) where the attacker reaches host child_process.execFileSync().

[LLM] vm2 NodeVM denylist bypass PoC strings — getBuiltinModule + inspector/promises Exploitation High
Hunts for the literal sandbox-escape primitives from CVE-2026-47140: `getBuiltinModule("child_process")`, `require("inspector/promises")`, and `Runtime.evaluate` posted via an Inspector Session. These strings appearing in script content, written .js files, or process command lines is direct evidence of exploitation or PoC testing. Rationale: PoC strings from the advisory body are uniquely diagnostic — `getBuiltinModule("child_process")` and `require("inspector/promises")` are the literal escape primitives and have effectively zero benign use in production Node.js. Falcon's ScriptControlScanInfo (AMSI integration) carries the raw script body, making it the highest-fidelity surface; Defender/Sentinel fall back to process-cmdline + .js file writes outside node_modules. Cross-checked with Semgrep's coverage of the four sibling vm2 escapes confirming these are the new bypass tokens in the 3.11.4 patch. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/vm2-nodejs-library-vulnerabilities.html • https://semgrep.dev/blog/2026/calling-back-to-vm2-and-escaping-sandbox/ • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rp36-8xq3-r6c4
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1480 T1211
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
let bypass_tokens = dynamic(["getBuiltinModule","inspector/promises","Runtime.evaluate","require('process').getBuiltinModule","require(\"process\").getBuiltinModule"]);
let proc_hits = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where FileName =~ "node.exe" or InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node.exe"
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any (bypass_tokens) or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (bypass_tokens)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, Source="ProcessEvents", Image=FolderPath, Cmd=ProcessCommandLine, ParentCmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256;
let file_hits = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
    | where FileName endswith ".js" or FileName endswith ".mjs" or FileName endswith ".cjs"
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("npm.cmd","yarn.cmd","pnpm.cmd","git.exe")
    | where FolderPath !contains @"\node_modules\"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, Source="FileEvents", Image=FolderPath, Cmd=tostring(strcat(FolderPath,"\\",FileName)), ParentCmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256;
proc_hits
| union file_hits
| order by Timestamp desc
let bypass_tokens = dynamic(["getBuiltinModule","inspector/promises","Runtime.evaluate"]);
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "node.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "node.exe" or TargetProcessName endswith "node.exe"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (bypass_tokens) or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any (bypass_tokens) or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any (bypass_tokens)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessCommandLine
| union (
    ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where EventType == "FileCreated" or EventType == "FileModified"
    | where TargetFileName endswith ".js" or TargetFileName endswith ".mjs" or TargetFileName endswith ".cjs"
    | where TargetFilePath !contains @"\node_modules\"
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (bypass_tokens)
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName=ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessCommandLine="", TargetProcessCommandLine=TargetFilePath
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Node.js process spawns shell or LOLBin — vm2 sandbox escape post-exploitation (CVE-2026-47210) Exploitation High
Hunts the universal vm2-escape pivot: a sandbox-escaped script reaches the host process and uses Node's child_process module to spawn cmd/powershell/sh/bash. The PoC for CVE-2026-47210 ends with `mainModule.require('child_process').execSync('touch pwned')` — any node.exe / node spawning a shell or scripting host is the high-fidelity signal because applications using vm2 as a security boundary should never have sandboxed code reach child_process. Rationale: Anchored on the exact post-escape sequence in the article's PoC: `e.constructor.constructor('return process')().mainModule.require('child_process').execSync(...)`. Once the JSPI bypass reaches host `process`, the attacker MUST cross from node into a child shell to do anything useful — there is no in-process payload step. Detection is article-grounded because vm2's whole purpose is preventing this; any node→shell parent-child is a sandbox failure. Cross-checked with Semgrep's vm2 escape write-up and TheHackerNews coverage which both confirm child_process as the universal pivot path. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6j2x-vhqr-qr7q • https://semgrep.dev/blog/2026/calling-back-to-vm2-and-escaping-sandbox/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/vm2-nodejs-library-vulnerabilities.html • https://www.kodemsecurity.com/resources/vm2-sandbox-escape-vulnerabilities-the-2026-cve-wave-turning-ai-agents-into-host-rce-vectors
ATT&CKT1059 T1068 T1611

| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","sh","bash","dash","zsh","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate

| where ParentProcessName endswith "node.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "/node" or ParentProcessName =~ "node"
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","sh","bash","dash","zsh","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe")

| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine,

          Hash = SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Vulnerable vm2 (<= 3.11.3) present on host — CVE-2026-47210 exposure Reconnaissance Medium
Inventory hunt for hosts running Node.js applications that bundle a vulnerable vm2 version. Looks for vm2 package directory writes under node_modules and TVM coverage of CVE-2026-47210. Used to scope the blast radius and prioritise patching before any escape detection fires. Rationale: Article names the exact affected package and version range: `npm:vm2 (vuln <= 3.11.3)`. This UC pivots on that fact two ways — TVM lookup by CveId (CVE-2026-47210) for managed inventory, and file-path evidence of node_modules/vm2 for any host the TVM scanner missed (containers, dev workstations, CI runners). Confirmed package + CVE mapping via the GHSA advisory and SCW/SC Media coverage. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6j2x-vhqr-qr7q • https://www.scworld.com/brief/critical-vm2-vulnerability-allows-sandbox-escape-and-arbitrary-code-execution • https://www.isec.news/2026/05/07/vm2-library-hit-by-a-dozen-critical-node-js-sandbox-escape-flaws/

[LLM] Node.js process spawning OS shell with enumeration commands — vm2 sandbox escape (CVE-2026-47137) Exploitation Medium
Hunts for node/node.exe directly spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, sh, or bash to execute reconnaissance commands (id, whoami, uname, /etc/passwd reads). This is the post-exploitation signature of a vm2 NodeVM sandbox escape via the nesting:true patch bypass, where attacker JS inside the sandbox reaches child_process.execSync on the host. The PoC in the advisory literally runs `id` via execSync. Rationale: Anchored on the advisory's PoC which spawns `child_process.execSync('id')` from inside the nested NodeVM. Node spawning a system shell is unusual outside of build tooling/CI; pairing the parent=node predicate with classic recon command-line tokens (whoami, id, uname, /etc/passwd) gives a high-fidelity post-exploit signal. CVE-2023-37903 (referenced in advisory) is the original sandbox escape this bypass revives. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8hg8-63c5-gwmx

id: 8a3f9b21-7e4c-4d1a-9f6b-2c5e8d4f1a30
description: Detects node/node.exe directly spawning a system shell that runs reconnaissance commands (whoami, id, uname, /etc/passwd reads), matching the post-exploitation footprint of a vm2 NodeVM sandbox escape via the nesting:true patch bypass (CVE-2026-47137, patch bypass of CVE-2023-37903).
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-m4wx-m65x-ghrr
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8hg8-63c5-gwmx
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/29
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.003
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1611
logsource:
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\node.exe'
      - '/node'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\wmic.exe'
      - '/sh'
      - '/bash'
      - '/dash'
      - '/zsh'
  selection_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'whoami'
      - 'uname'
      - 'hostname'
      - 'ipconfig'
      - 'ifconfig'
      - '/etc/passwd'
      - '/etc/shadow'
      - 'child_process'
      - 'execSync'
      - 'net user'
      - 'systeminfo'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate Node.js applications that shell out for environment detection (uname, hostname)
  - DevOps/CI Node tooling that wraps shell commands
  - Node-based system administration utilities
level: high
source:(windows.sysmon OR linux.auditd) (@ParentImage:(*\\node.exe OR *\\Node.exe OR *\\NODE.EXE) OR @process.parent.executable.path:(*/node OR */NODE) OR @ParentBaseFileName:(node.exe OR node)) (@Image:(*\\cmd.exe OR *\\CMD.EXE OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\PWSH.EXE OR *\\wmic.exe) OR @process.executable.path:(*/sh OR */bash OR */dash OR */zsh)) (@CommandLine:(*whoami* OR *uname* OR *hostname* OR *ipconfig* OR *ifconfig* OR *child_process* OR *execSync* OR *"/etc/passwd"* OR *"/etc/shadow"* OR *systeminfo*) OR @process.command_line:(*whoami* OR *uname* OR *hostname* OR *"/etc/passwd"* OR *"/etc/shadow"* OR *child_process* OR *execSync*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/^node(\.exe)?$/i
| ImageFileName=/\\(cmd|powershell|pwsh|wmic)\.exe$|\/(sh|bash|dash|zsh|ash)$/i
| regex("whoami|\\buname\\b|hostname|ipconfig|ifconfig|\\/etc\\/passwd|\\/etc\\/shadow|child_process|execSync|systeminfo|net user", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

[LLM] Vulnerable vm2 package (<=3.11.3) present on host — CVE-2026-47137 exposure surface Weaponization High
Hunts for vm2 npm package installs on endpoints/servers — the package's package.json under any node_modules\vm2 path. vm2 was deprecated and ANY version <=3.11.3 is vulnerable to the nesting:true patch bypass that produces full RCE. Use this to inventory exposure for the CVE-2026-47137 mitigation campaign. Rationale: The advisory explicitly names the vulnerable package (npm:vm2 <=3.11.3) and the patched-but-bypassed file (nodevm.js line 263). File-presence telemetry for node_modules/vm2/package.json gives a complete exposure inventory; nodevm.js presence is a precision pivot to the exact vulnerable code path. Triage on file content/version is a follow-up step the SOC runs after the hunt surfaces hosts. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8hg8-63c5-gwmx
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(90d)
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\node_modules\vm2\", "/node_modules/vm2/")
| where FileName in~ ("package.json", "nodevm.js", "main.js", "index.js")
| summarize FirstSeen = min(Timestamp),
            LastSeen  = max(Timestamp),
            Paths     = make_set(FolderPath, 20),
            Files     = make_set(FileName, 10),
            Writers   = make_set(InitiatingProcessFileName, 10)
  by DeviceName
| extend NodeAppHost = iff(array_length(Paths) > 0, true, false)
| order by LastSeen desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
| where TargetFilePath has_any ("\\node_modules\\vm2\\", "/node_modules/vm2/")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("package.json", "nodevm.js", "main.js", "index.js")
| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen  = max(TimeGenerated),
            Paths     = make_set(TargetFilePath, 20),
            Files     = make_set(TargetFileName, 10),
            Writers   = make_set(ActingProcessName, 10)
  by DvcHostname
| order by LastSeen desc

// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-47137", "CVE-2023-37903")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-47137", "CVE-2023-37903")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

[LLM] Vulnerable vm2 package (<=3.11.3) present on endpoints — CVE-2026-47208 exposure Weaponization High
Hunts file-system evidence of the vm2 npm package at vulnerable versions deployed on hosts. The PoC requires the vm2 module to be loaded; any node_modules/vm2/package.json on disk with version <= 3.11.3 is a direct exposure indicator. Use this to bound the vulnerable surface before behavioral hunts. Rationale: Article explicitly names affected package as 'npm:vm2 (vuln <= 3.11.3)'. Detecting node_modules/vm2/package.json on disk is the cleanest exposure indicator before behavioral exploitation. Corroborated against vm2 GitHub advisory and TheHackerNews 2026 vm2 wave write-up. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/patriksimek/vm2/security/advisories/GHSA-qvjj-29qf-hp7p • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/vm2-nodejs-library-vulnerabilities.html • https://advisories.gitlab.com/npm/vm2/CVE-2026-24120/
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
// Hunts vm2 package.json drops on disk; pair with DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory if Node modules ingested
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "package.json"
| where FolderPath has @"\node_modules\vm2\" or FolderPath has "/node_modules/vm2/"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// ASIM file-event variant — covers vendors shipping file telemetry to Sentinel
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFileName =~ "package.json"
| where TargetFilePath has @"\node_modules\vm2\" or TargetFilePath has "/node_modules/vm2/"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] node.exe spawning child_process targets — vm2 Promise species sandbox escape post-exploitation Exploitation Medium
Detects the post-escape pattern from CVE-2026-47208 PoC where the attacker uses ex.constructor.constructor('return process')().mainModule.require('child_process').execSync(...) to spawn arbitrary host processes from inside a vm2 sandbox. Filters for node.exe parent spawning shells/cmd/touch/curl/wget without a benign build-tool ancestor. Rationale: PoC ends in 'ex.constructor.constructor("return process")().mainModule.require(\'child_process\').execSync(\'touch pwned\')'. The detectable observable is node.exe parent spawning child_process targets without a benign npm/yarn/electron build-tool ancestor. Corroborated against TheHackerNews 2026 vm2 wave coverage and Kodem analysis of AI-agent RCE risk. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/patriksimek/vm2/security/advisories/GHSA-qvjj-29qf-hp7p • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/vm2-nodejs-library-vulnerabilities.html • https://www.kodemsecurity.com/resources/vm2-sandbox-escape-vulnerabilities-the-2026-cve-wave-turning-ai-agents-into-host-rce-vectors
ATT&CKT1068 T1059.007 T1059.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
// vm2 sandbox escape -> child_process.execSync spawns host process from node.exe
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node.exe"
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","touch.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm install","npm ci","npm run","yarn install","pnpm install","node-gyp","electron-builder","husky","postinstall"))
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentPath = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd  = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildPath  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd   = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256, ProcessIntegrityLevel
| order by Timestamp desc
// ASIM process-create — node.exe parent spawning shell/cmd/touch after vm2 escape
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName endswith "node.exe"
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","touch.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","certutil.exe")
| where not (ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm install","npm ci","npm run","yarn","pnpm","node-gyp","electron","postinstall","husky"))
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine,
          TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Node.js Spawning Shell/Touch Post-vm2 Sandbox Escape (CVE-2026-47208)
id: 8e4f2c1a-9b3d-4e6f-a82c-1f5d6e9c3b47
description: Detects node.exe spawning shells, touch, curl, or LOLBins — the post-escape behavioural signature of CVE-2026-47208 vm2 Promise species sandbox escape via child_process.execSync.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-76w7-j9cq-rx2j
  - https://github.com/patriksimek/vm2/security/advisories/GHSA-qvjj-29qf-hp7p
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/29
tags:
  - attack.t1068
  - attack.t1059.007
  - attack.t1059.003
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  parent:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\node.exe'
  child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\bash.exe'
      - '\sh.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
      - '\touch.exe'
      - '\curl.exe'
      - '\wget.exe'
      - '\certutil.exe'
  filter_npm:
    ParentCommandLine|contains:
      - 'npm install'
      - 'npm ci'
      - 'npm run'
      - 'yarn'
      - 'pnpm'
      - 'node-gyp'
      - 'postinstall'
      - 'husky'
      - 'electron'
  condition: parent and child and not filter_npm
falsepositives:
  - npm/yarn/pnpm postinstall lifecycle scripts (filtered via parent cmdline)
  - Electron app helpers spawning native helpers

[LLM] vm2 Promise species sandbox escape PoC fingerprint in scripts/command lines Weaponization High
Hunts the specific JavaScript exploitation idiom from CVE-2026-47208 PoC: combinations of Symbol.species class extension of Promise, ex.constructor.constructor('return process')(), and mainModule.require('child_process'). These strings appear in attacker payloads delivered to vm2-using services and in saved exploit files. Rationale: The PoC contains highly distinctive idioms: 'ex.constructor.constructor("return process")()' for breaking out via the prototype chain, 'mainModule.require(\'child_process\')' for arbitrary execution, and 'Symbol.species' class extension of Promise — the actual vulnerable mechanism. These three strings together are extremely rare in benign code. Sigma omitted because the detection chains union/joins across cmdline and file telemetry — single-event shape doesn't fit. Corroborated against the GitHub advisory PoC and GitLab CVE-2026-24120 advisory of the same Promise.species root cause. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-76w7-j9cq-rx2j • https://advisories.gitlab.com/npm/vm2/CVE-2026-24120/ • https://github.com/patriksimek/vm2/security/advisories/GHSA-qvjj-29qf-hp7p
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1068

// Hunts CVE-2026-47208 PoC fingerprint in node.exe cmdlines AND .js file drops
let poc_strings = dynamic([
    "constructor.constructor(\"return process\")",
    "constructor.constructor('return process')",
    "mainModule.require('child_process')",
    "mainModule.require(\"child_process\")",
    "Symbol.species"
]);
let cmdline_hits =
    DeviceProcessEvents

    | where FileName in~ ("node.exe","nodejs.exe")

let file_hits =

    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName,
              Source = "file",

| order by Timestamp desc

[LLM] vm2 sandbox-escape PoC strings observed in inbound HTTP request body / WAF Exploitation High
Hunts the exact JavaScript token sequence from the CVE-2026-47131 PoC (Buffer.call.call/__lookupGetter__/__lookupSetter__ + WebAssembly.compileStreaming + e.constructor.constructor + mainModule.require) in web request URLs and bodies traversing the WAF / reverse proxy. Targets any service that hands user-supplied JS to a vm2 sandbox. Rationale: PoC body in the advisory cites the exact strings Buffer.call.call({}.__lookupGetter__, Buffer, "__proto__"), WebAssembly.compileStreaming(), e.constructor.constructor, and new HostFunction("return process")().mainModule.require("child_process").execSync — those tokens together don't appear in legitimate JSON payloads or REST API traffic. The narrow string set keeps FPs near zero. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-v6mx-mf47-r5wg • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-47131
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.007
Data sourcesWeb.Web
// Defender has no inbound HTTP-body table; pivot via DeviceNetworkEvents to Node processes that received the payload then look at child shells
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node.exe"
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","wmic.exe","mshta.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("echo pwned","child_process","execSync")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
let PocTokens = dynamic(["__lookupGetter__","__lookupSetter__","Buffer.call.call","compileStreaming","e.constructor.constructor","mainModule.require","child_process\").execSync"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(
  CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where Message has_any (PocTokens) or RequestURL has_any (PocTokens) or RequestContext has_any (PocTokens) or RequestCookies has_any (PocTokens)
  | project TimeGenerated, Source="CEF", DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, SourceIP=SourceIP, DestinationIP, Url=RequestURL, Method=RequestMethod, Evidence=coalesce(Message, RequestURL)
),
(
  W3CIISLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where csUriQuery has_any (PocTokens) or csUriStem has_any (PocTokens) or csUserAgent has_any (PocTokens)
  | project TimeGenerated, Source="IIS", DeviceVendor="Microsoft", DeviceProduct="IIS", SourceIP=cIP, DestinationIP="", Url=strcat(csUriStem, "?", csUriQuery), Method=csMethod, Evidence=csUriQuery
),
(
  ImWebSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where Url has_any (PocTokens) or UrlOriginal has_any (PocTokens) or HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent has_any (PocTokens)
  | project TimeGenerated, Source="ASIM", DeviceVendor=EventVendor, DeviceProduct=EventProduct, SourceIP=SrcIpAddr, DestinationIP=DstIpAddr, Url, Method=HttpMethod, Evidence=Url
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Node.exe spawning OS shell after vm2 sandbox exploitation Installation High
Hunts the post-exploit signature of CVE-2026-47131: a Node.js process spawning cmd/powershell/bash/sh with command lines containing the PoC's distinctive 'echo pwned' marker or child_process.execSync invocations. Node legitimately shells out occasionally for build tooling, so we anchor on the PoC string and the unusual integrity-level / parent-tree combination. Rationale: The PoC ends with execSync("echo pwned", { stdio: "inherit" }) — a near-unique marker — preceded by mainModule.require("child_process"). The node→shell parent-child plus those two string tokens together is article-specific and won't fire on normal Node build steps. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-v6mx-mf47-r5wg

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files

Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] The Gentlemen ransomware 'gentlemen_system' SYSTEM scheduled task creation Installation High
Detects creation/registration of a scheduled task literally named 'gentlemen_system' which The Gentlemen ransomware (Storm-2697) uses to re-launch its encryptor under the SYSTEM account for elevated local-drive encryption. The article notes operators first delete any existing task of that name then register and immediately trigger a fresh one. Rationale: Anchored on the verbatim task name 'gentlemen_system' from the article and Microsoft's report. The task name is build-specific and not used by any known benign tool, so a single match is high-fidelity. Cross-checked Microsoft Threat Intelligence (Storm-2697) and MITRE T1053.005 / T1548. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1053/005/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1548/
ATT&CKT1053.005 T1548
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FileName =~ "schtasks.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "gentlemen_system")
   or (FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has "gentlemen_system" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Register-ScheduledTask","New-ScheduledTask","schtasks"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, AccountDomain, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4698
| where EventData has "gentlemen_system" or TargetUserName has "gentlemen_system" or CommandLine has "gentlemen_system"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, SubjectDomainName, TargetUserName, CommandLine, EventData
| union (
    SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where (NewProcessName endswith "\\schtasks.exe" and CommandLine has "gentlemen_system")
       or (NewProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") and CommandLine has "gentlemen_system")
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, CommandLine, NewProcessName, ParentProcessName
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: The Gentlemen Ransomware gentlemen_system Scheduled Task Creation
id: 8e2d7f4a-1b3c-4d5e-9f6a-0b1c2d3e4f5a
description: Detects creation of the SYSTEM-privileged scheduled task 'gentlemen_system' used by The Gentlemen (Storm-2697) ransomware to encrypt local drives with elevated privileges.
references:
  - https://cybersecuritynews.com/ransomware-uses-system-scheduled-task/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/30
tags:
  - attack.t1053.005
  - attack.t1548
  - attack.privilege_escalation
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_schtasks:
    Image|endswith: '\schtasks.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'gentlemen_system'
  selection_powershell:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: 'gentlemen_system'
  condition: selection_schtasks or selection_powershell
level: critical
(source:windows.security OR source:windows.sysmon) (@EventID:(4688 OR 4698 OR 1)) (@CommandLine:*gentlemen_system* OR @CommandLine:*GENTLEMEN_SYSTEM* OR @EventData:*gentlemen_system*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\\(schtasks|powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/i
| regex("gentlemen_system", field=CommandLine, flags="i")
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="schtasks.exe" OR Processes.process_name="powershell.exe" OR Processes.process_name="pwsh.exe") (Processes.process="*gentlemen_system*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_id | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where match(process, "(?i)/create|/run|register-scheduledtask|new-scheduledtask") | sort - lastTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="schtasks.exe" OR Processes.process_name="powershell.exe" OR Processes.process_name="pwsh.exe") (Processes.process="*gentlemen_system*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_id | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where match(process, "(?i)/create|/run|register-scheduledtask|new-scheduledtask") | sort - lastTime
[LLM] The Gentlemen ransomware UpdateSystem/UpdateUser persistence scheduled tasks Installation High
Detects creation of the 'UpdateSystem' (SYSTEM context) and 'UpdateUser' (current-user context) scheduled tasks that The Gentlemen ransomware uses for boot persistence. Distinct from the gentlemen_system runtime escalation task: these survive reboot and re-launch the encryptor. Rationale: Task names UpdateSystem and UpdateUser are listed verbatim in the article's IOC table as Storm-2697 persistence mechanisms. The names mimic legitimate Windows Update naming so an analyst-grade filter against MoUsoCoreWorker/TiWorker is required to suppress benign Windows Update task creations. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1053/005/
ATT&CKT1053.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "schtasks.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("UpdateSystem","UpdateUser")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/Create","-Create","/SC","/TN")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MoUsoCoreWorker.exe","TiWorker.exe","wuauclt.exe","svchost.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "WindowsUpdate"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4698
| extend TaskName = tostring(extract(@"TaskName\">([^<]+)", 1, EventData))
| where TaskName in~ ("\\UpdateSystem","UpdateSystem","\\UpdateUser","UpdateUser")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, SubjectDomainName, TaskName, EventData
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: The Gentlemen Ransomware UpdateSystem/UpdateUser Persistence Task
id: 4c1d8e2b-7f3a-4b9c-8d5e-1a2b3c4d5e6f
description: Detects creation of UpdateSystem (SYSTEM) or UpdateUser persistence scheduled tasks used by The Gentlemen ransomware to re-launch its payload at boot.
references:
  - https://cybersecuritynews.com/ransomware-uses-system-scheduled-task/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/30
tags:
  - attack.t1053.005
  - attack.persistence
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\schtasks.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '/Create'
  taskname:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'UpdateSystem'
      - 'UpdateUser'
  filter_wu:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\MoUsoCoreWorker.exe'
      - '\TiWorker.exe'
      - '\wuauclt.exe'
  condition: selection and taskname and not filter_wu
level: high
source:windows.security @EventID:4698 (@EventData:*UpdateSystem* OR @EventData:*UpdateUser*) -@EventData:*MoUsoCoreWorker* -@EventData:*WindowsUpdate*
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\\schtasks\.exe$/i
| regex("/(Create|TN)", field=CommandLine, flags="i")
| regex("UpdateSystem|UpdateUser", field=CommandLine)
| NOT ParentBaseFileName=/(MoUsoCoreWorker|TiWorker|wuauclt|svchost)\.exe/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="schtasks.exe" (Processes.process="*UpdateSystem*" OR Processes.process="*UpdateUser*") (Processes.process="*/Create*" OR Processes.process="*/RU*SYSTEM*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where NOT match(parent_process_name, "(?i)(wuauclt|TiWorker|MoUsoCoreWorker|wsusservice)\.exe") | sort - lastTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="schtasks.exe" (Processes.process="*UpdateSystem*" OR Processes.process="*UpdateUser*") (Processes.process="*/Create*" OR Processes.process="*/RU*SYSTEM*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where NOT match(parent_process_name, "(?i)(wuauclt|TiWorker|MoUsoCoreWorker|wsusservice)\.exe") | sort - lastTime
[LLM] The Gentlemen ransomware GupdateS/GupdateU autorun registry persistence Installation High
Detects creation of the GupdateS (HKLM) or GupdateU (HKCU) registry values under Run autostart keys — system-wide and user-scoped persistence anchors used by The Gentlemen ransomware. Distinct pivot from the scheduled-task persistence: registry-event telemetry rather than schtasks.exe execution. Rationale: GupdateS and GupdateU are verbatim IOC value names from the article's IOC table, scoped to HKLM and HKCU Run keys. The names are not used by any known benign software (Google Update uses 'gupdate' service but not 'GupdateS'/'GupdateU' as Run-key value names), making a single hit very high-confidence. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1547/001/
ATT&CKT1547.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryKeyCreated")
| where RegistryValueName in~ ("GupdateS","GupdateU")
   or (RegistryKey has_any (@"\Run", @"\RunOnce") and RegistryValueName has_any ("GupdateS","GupdateU"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessSHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where RegistryValue in~ ("GupdateS","GupdateU")
   or (RegistryKey has_any (@"\Run", @"\RunOnce") and RegistryValue has_any ("GupdateS","GupdateU"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, RegistryKey, RegistryValue, RegistryValueData, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: The Gentlemen Ransomware GupdateS/GupdateU Registry Persistence
id: 7a9e3b5c-2d4f-4e8a-9b1c-3d5e7f8a9b0c
description: Detects creation of GupdateS (HKLM) or GupdateU (HKCU) Run-key autostart values used by The Gentlemen ransomware for boot persistence.
references:

author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/30
tags:
  - attack.t1547.001
  - attack.persistence
logsource:
  category: registry_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetObject|contains:
      - '\CurrentVersion\Run\'
      - '\CurrentVersion\RunOnce\'
  value:
    TargetObject|endswith:
      - '\GupdateS'
      - '\GupdateU'
  condition: selection and value
level: critical
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:13 (@TargetObject:(*\\Run\\GupdateS OR *\\Run\\GupdateU OR *\\RunOnce\\GupdateS OR *\\RunOnce\\GupdateU OR *\\run\\GupdateS OR *\\run\\GupdateU))
#event_simpleName=AsepValueUpdate
| RegValueName=/^Gupdate[SU]$/
| regex("\\\\Run(Once)?\\\\?$", field=RegObjectName, flags="i")
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, RegObjectName, RegValueName, RegStringValue, ContextImageFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry where (Registry.registry_value_name="GupdateS" OR Registry.registry_value_name="GupdateU") (Registry.registry_path="*\\Run\\*" OR Registry.registry_path="*\\RunOnce\\*" OR Registry.registry_key_name="*\\Run" OR Registry.registry_key_name="*\\RunOnce") by Registry.dest Registry.user Registry.registry_path Registry.registry_value_name Registry.registry_value_data Registry.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)` | sort - lastTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry where (Registry.registry_value_name="GupdateS" OR Registry.registry_value_name="GupdateU") (Registry.registry_path="*\\Run\\*" OR Registry.registry_path="*\\RunOnce\\*" OR Registry.registry_key_name="*\\Run" OR Registry.registry_key_name="*\\RunOnce") by Registry.dest Registry.user Registry.registry_path Registry.registry_value_name Registry.registry_value_data Registry.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)` | sort - lastTime
[LLM] The Gentlemen ransomware .umc16h extension and README-GENTLEMEN.txt drops Actions on Objectives High
Detects mass file rename to the '.umc16h' extension and concurrent drops of 'README-GENTLEMEN.txt' ransom notes — the active encryption phase of The Gentlemen ransomware. Bursty per-host file-create signal scoped on extension + note filename. Rationale: Anchored on three verbatim IOC strings from the article: extension '.umc16h', filename 'README-GENTLEMEN.txt', wallpaper 'gentlemen.bmp', and 'wipefile.tmp'. Threshold of >=10 encrypted files in 5min reduces noise from analyst sandbox tests while still catching real outbreaks; ransom-note drop alone is alert-worthy at >=3. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1486/
ATT&CKT1486 T1485
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed")
| where FileName endswith ".umc16h"
   or FileName =~ "README-GENTLEMEN.txt"
   or FileName =~ "gentlemen.bmp"
   or FileName =~ "wipefile.tmp"
| summarize EncryptedCount = countif(FileName endswith ".umc16h"),
            NoteCount     = countif(FileName =~ "README-GENTLEMEN.txt"),
            WallpaperHit  = countif(FileName =~ "gentlemen.bmp"),
            WipeHit       = countif(FileName =~ "wipefile.tmp"),
            FirstSeen     = min(Timestamp),
            LastSeen      = max(Timestamp),
            SampleFolders = make_set(FolderPath, 10),
            Initiators    = make_set(InitiatingProcessFileName, 5),
            InitiatorHashes = make_set(InitiatingProcessSHA256, 5)
            by DeviceName, bin(Timestamp, 5m)
| where EncryptedCount >= 10 or NoteCount >= 3 or WallpaperHit > 0 or WipeHit > 0
| order by FirstSeen desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFileExtension =~ "umc16h"
   or TargetFileName =~ "README-GENTLEMEN.txt"
   or TargetFileName =~ "gentlemen.bmp"
   or TargetFileName =~ "wipefile.tmp"
| summarize EncryptedCount = countif(TargetFileExtension =~ "umc16h"),
            NoteCount     = countif(TargetFileName =~ "README-GENTLEMEN.txt"),
            WallpaperHit  = countif(TargetFileName =~ "gentlemen.bmp"),
            FirstSeen     = min(TimeGenerated),
            Actors        = make_set(ActorUsername, 5),
            Processes     = make_set(ActingProcessName, 5)
            by DvcHostname, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where EncryptedCount >= 10 or NoteCount >= 3 or WallpaperHit > 0
| order by FirstSeen desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 (@TargetFilename:*.umc16h OR @TargetFilename:*\\README-GENTLEMEN.txt OR @TargetFilename:*\\gentlemen.bmp OR @TargetFilename:*\\wipefile.tmp OR @TargetFilename:*\\WIPEFILE.TMP)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| regex("\\.umc16h$|\\\\README-GENTLEMEN\\.txt$|\\\\gentlemen\\.bmp$|\\\\wipefile\\.tmp$", field=TargetFileName, flags="i")
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName], function={ 
    EncryptedCount := count(field=TargetFileName, where=regex("\\.umc16h$", field=TargetFileName, flags="i")) 
    | NoteCount := count(field=TargetFileName, where=regex("README-GENTLEMEN\\.txt$", field=TargetFileName, flags="i"))
  })
| EncryptedCount > 10 OR NoteCount > 2
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as paths from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_name="*.umc16h" OR Filesystem.file_name="README-GENTLEMEN.txt" OR Filesystem.file_name="gentlemen.bmp" OR Filesystem.file_name="wipefile.tmp") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name span=5m | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where count > 10 | sort - lastTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as paths from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_name="*.umc16h" OR Filesystem.file_name="README-GENTLEMEN.txt" OR Filesystem.file_name="gentlemen.bmp" OR Filesystem.file_name="wipefile.tmp") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name span=5m | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where count > 10 | sort - lastTime
[LLM] The Gentlemen ransomware PsExec staging at C:\Temp\psexec.exe for lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
Detects PsExec (or PsExec-renamed) execution from the article's specific staging path C:\Temp\psexec.exe, optionally combined with writes of psexec.exe to admin shares (C$, ADMIN$). This is The Gentlemen's lateral-movement stage — the binary is dropped to C:\Temp then propagated. Rationale: Article IOC table lists C:\Temp\psexec.exe as the literal staging path for lateral movement. Path-anchored detection avoids the FP-storm of generic 'psexec.exe' alerts. Combined file-event arm catches admin-share propagation (the article explicitly lists 8 lateral-move methods including PsExec and admin-share staging). Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1570/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
ATT&CKT1570 T1021.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
let PsExecAtTemp = DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FolderPath =~ @"C:\Temp\psexec.exe"
   or (FileName =~ "psexec.exe" and FolderPath startswith @"C:\Temp\")
   or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath =~ @"C:\Temp\psexec.exe" and InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "psexec.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, SHA256;
let PsExecToAdminShare = DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "psexec.exe" or FileName endswith ".exe" and InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "psexec.exe"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\C$\", @"\ADMIN$\", @"\IPC$\")
   or RequestProtocol == "SMB"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessSHA256, RemoteIP=RequestSourceIP;
PsExecAtTemp
| union PsExecToAdminShare
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName =~ @"C:\Temp\psexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\\psexec.exe" and NewProcessName startswith @"C:\Temp\")
   or (ParentProcessName =~ @"C:\Temp\psexec.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] The Gentlemen ransomware encryptor SHA256 hash execution Installation High
High-confidence alerting detection on the exact SHA256 of The Gentlemen encryptor binary (Storm-2697) — fires on process execution, file write, or image load of the known-bad hash. Rationale: Direct SHA256 from the article IOC table and verbatim code block. Hash-based detections have near-zero FP rate (only the exact binary matches) but degrade over time as operators recompile — pair with the behavioural UCs in this set for durable coverage. Cross-referenced Microsoft Threat Intelligence Storm-2697 tracking. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1486/ • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
let BadHash = "22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67";
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where SHA256 =~ BadHash or InitiatingProcessSHA256 =~ BadHash
| project Source="Process", Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessSHA256
| union (
    DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where SHA256 =~ BadHash or InitiatingProcessSHA256 =~ BadHash
    | project Source="FileWrite", Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessSHA256
)
| union (
    DeviceImageLoadEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where SHA256 =~ BadHash
    | project Source="ImageLoad", Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName
)
| order by Timestamp desc
let BadHash = "22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67";
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where Hash =~ BadHash or SHA256 =~ BadHash
| project Source="Process", TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, Hash
| union (
    ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where TargetFileSHA256 =~ BadHash
    | project Source="FileWrite", TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, Hash=TargetFileSHA256
)
| union (
    SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where EventID == 4688 and FileHash has BadHash
    | project Source="4688", TimeGenerated, DvcHostname=Computer, ActorUsername=SubjectUserName, ActingProcessName=NewProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine=CommandLine, Hash=FileHash
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: The Gentlemen Ransomware Encryptor SHA256 Match
id: 9f1a2b3c-4d5e-6f7a-8b9c-0d1e2f3a4b5c

(source:windows.sysmon OR source:windows.defender) (@Hashes:*22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67* OR @SHA256:22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67 OR @FileHash:22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67)

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d07
status: experimental
description: |

    cscript, mshta, rundll32, regsvr32 — classic macro / embedded-
    object payload signature.
references:

author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059
    - attack.t1566.001
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\winword.exe'
            - '\excel.exe'
            - '\powerpnt.exe'
            - '\outlook.exe'
            - '\onenote.exe'
            - '\mspub.exe'
            - '\visio.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate automation macros in trusted internal documents
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host

| order by files desc

| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc

| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc
