File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67") or SHA1 in~ ("22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67") or MD5 in~ ("22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67") or SHA1 in~ ("22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67") or MD5 in~ ("22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] JINX-0164 C2 and payload delivery infrastructure callback · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] nord-stream CI/CD secret-exfiltration tool execution · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
[LLM] JINX-0164 AUDIOFIX/MINIRAT macOS LaunchAgent plist persistence Installation High
Detects creation of the three specific LaunchAgent plist filenames JINX-0164 uses to persist AUDIOFIX (com.microsoft.teams.coreaudiod, io.aircall.workspace.helper) and MINIRAT (com.apple.Terminal.profiler). These names impersonate legitimate vendors but the exact strings are unique to this campaign per Wiz CIRT. Rationale: Anchored on three exact plist filenames called out in the Wiz CIRT IOC table (com.microsoft.teams.coreaudiod.plist, io.aircall.workspace.helper.plist, com.apple.Terminal.profiler.plist) under ~/Library/LaunchAgents/. Each name impersonates a legit vendor but in that exact spelling is unique to JINX-0164 - very low base rate.
ATT&CKT1543.001 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FolderPath has "/Library/LaunchAgents/"
| where FileName in~ ("com.microsoft.teams.coreaudiod.plist","io.aircall.workspace.helper.plist","com.apple.Terminal.profiler.plist")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessSHA256, SHA256, ActionType
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFilePath has "/Library/LaunchAgents/"
| where TargetFileName in~ ("com.microsoft.teams.coreaudiod.plist","io.aircall.workspace.helper.plist","com.apple.Terminal.profiler.plist")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFileSHA256, EventType
| order by TimeGenerated desc

id: 7a8c4f9e-1d3a-4b62-9c8e-2f5a6e7b3c11
description: Detects creation of LaunchAgent plist files matching the JINX-0164 AUDIOFIX/MINIRAT persistence filenames documented by Wiz CIRT.

[LLM] JINX-0164 C2 and payload delivery infrastructure callback Command & Control High
Hunts outbound connectivity to the AUDIOFIX/MINIRAT C2 domains (datahub.ink, cloud-sync.online, byte-io.us), payload delivery domains (apple.driver-store.com, apple.driver-update.io, driver-updater.net, driver-hub.net, drvstore.com) and their resolved IPs. Any single hit is a hard alert. Rationale: Anchored on the full Wiz CIRT IOC list - 8 IPs and 14 domains. Even one hit is high-fidelity; combined query covers DNS, direct-IP TCP, proxy/CSL telemetry. CloudTrail variant catches stolen-AWS-key usage from JINX-0164 infrastructure.

[LLM] Trojanized npm @velora-dex/sdk v4.9.1 install or import Delivery High
Detects developer or CI/CD hosts installing or referencing the trojanized version 4.9.1 of @velora-dex/sdk. JINX-0164 appended code to this single version that fetches a shell script and drops MINIRAT. Rationale: Wiz CIRT named the exact package and exact version (@velora-dex/sdk 4.9.1, published 2026-04-07). Bundles process exec (npm/yarn install/add) and lockfile writes - both surfaces a developer would hit. Version 4.9.0 and 4.9.2+ are clean, so the version-specific predicate is the high-fidelity anchor.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
union isfuzzy=true
(DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(60d)
  | where FileName in~ ("npm","yarn","pnpm","npx","node","npm.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.cmd")
  | where ProcessCommandLine has "@velora-dex/sdk" and ProcessCommandLine has "4.9.1"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath),
(DeviceFileEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(60d)
  | where FileName in~ ("package.json","package-lock.json","yarn.lock","pnpm-lock.yaml")
  | where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "@velora-dex/sdk" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "4.9.1"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath)
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("npm","yarn","pnpm","npx","node") or TargetProcessName has_any ("npm","yarn","pnpm","npx","node")
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has "@velora-dex/sdk" and TargetProcessCommandLine has "4.9.1"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] User access to JINX-0164 fake conferencing platform domains (Teams/Slack/Bitget spoofs) Delivery High
Detects URL clicks or browser navigation to the JINX-0164 meeting-spoofing domains used to lure LinkedIn-recruited developers into downloading the macOS dropper. These domains impersonate Teams, Slack, Bitget and generic conferencing URLs. Rationale: Six lookalike domains called out explicitly in the Wiz IOC table - teamicrosoft.com is a clear Teams typosquat, us03-slack.online mimics Slack subdomain, bitget-meeting.com targets the named crypto-exchange user base. Cross-source union catches click (Safe Links), navigation (DeviceNetworkEvents) and perimeter proxy.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1656
Data sourcesWeb.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
let SpoofDomains = dynamic(["bitget-meeting.com","teamicrosoft.com","teams.cam","live.us.org","us03-slack.online","live.ong"]);
let ClickHits = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where Url has_any (SpoofDomains)
    | project Timestamp, AccountUpn, Url, ActionType, IPAddress, NetworkMessageId, Source="UrlClickEvents";
let NetHits = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where RemoteUrl has_any (SpoofDomains)
    | project Timestamp, AccountUpn=InitiatingProcessAccountUpn, Url=RemoteUrl, ActionType, IPAddress=RemoteIP, NetworkMessageId="", Source="DeviceNetworkEvents", DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
union isfuzzy=true ClickHits, NetHits
| order by Timestamp desc
let SpoofDomains = dynamic(["bitget-meeting.com","teamicrosoft.com","teams.cam","live.us.org","us03-slack.online","live.ong"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(ImWebSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where Url has_any (SpoofDomains) or HttpHostName in~ (SpoofDomains)
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, Url, HttpHostName, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, EventVendor),
(CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where RequestURL has_any (SpoofDomains) or DestinationHostName in~ (SpoofDomains)
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname=DeviceName, SrcIpAddr=SourceIP, SrcUsername=SourceUserName, Url=RequestURL, HttpHostName=DestinationHostName, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent=RequestClientApplication, EventVendor=DeviceVendor)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] nord-stream CI/CD secret-exfiltration tool execution Actions on Objectives Medium
Hunts for execution of nord-stream, the open-source GitHub Actions secret-pulling tool the article cites JINX-0164 abusing after stealing GitHub PATs. Looks for both direct binary execution and python -m / pipx invocations. Rationale: Tool is named explicitly in the article as JINX-0164's tradecraft for pulling CI/CD secrets after PAT theft. Filename/binary + commandline coverage. Marked hunting (not alerting) because red teams legitimately use nord-stream; the FP-suppression on --help/--version trims one common noise case. Pair with GitHub audit log review to confirm intent.
ATT&CKT1552.004 T1213.003 T1567
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(90d)
| where FileName in~ ("nord-stream","nord-stream.py","nord_stream.py")
    or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("nord-stream","nord_stream")
    or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("nord-stream","nord_stream")
| where not(ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--help","-h "," -V","--version"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("nord-stream","nord_stream")
    or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("nord-stream","nord_stream")
    or TargetProcessName has_any ("nord-stream","nord_stream.py")
| where not(TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("--help","-h ","--version"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

External Teams chat where displayName contains 'helpdesk' or 'IT support' — common 2024+ vishing pattern (Storm-1811, Black Basta, UNC6692). No CIM data model maps to Teams chats; uses raw O365 audit logs.

Data sourcesCloudAppEvents

| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application == "Microsoft Teams"
| where ActionType == "MessageSent"
| where RawEventData has "ExternalParticipants"
| extend SenderDisplayName = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).SenderDisplayName)
| where SenderDisplayName matches regex @"(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, IPAddress, ActivityType, SenderDisplayName, RawEventData
// External Teams chat — Teams audit lives in OfficeActivity.
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OfficeWorkload == "MicrosoftTeams"
| where Operation in~ ("MessageSent","ChatCreated","TeamsImpersonationDetected")
| where isnotempty(UserId)
| where Subject has_any ("IT","helpdesk","support","password","verify")
   or Recipients has_any ("IT","helpdesk")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, Operation, Subject, Recipients,
          ClientIP, UserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc

`o365_management_activity`

logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\AnyDesk.exe'
            - '\TeamViewer.exe'
            - '\TeamViewer_Service.exe'
            - '\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe'
            - '\ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe'
            - '\atera_agent.exe'
            - '\SplashtopStreamer.exe'
            - '\RustDesk.exe'
            - '\NinjaOne.exe'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - IT-approved RMM in use across the estate. Maintain a known-IT-
      tool exclusion list per environment.
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe","kaseya*.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe","kaseya*.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

let BadHashes = dynamic(["0a8ab3d16b12d3a453ee5a3208fe04744ad54514ef8ea27bb8fe32679efad270", "0b028b781950641818800fee2b4bf68e4ef2bcee53fe71a21755275ba10875f5", "a35d2b67fa478a7174e308b43ce30bf69b3bc6f44fa76197fdf95fc2fbc1cf7d", "65cba741fe30fa4799fb9002ea8de6d96042a59159dd7c3419c766af24c7a8b4", "0b1a36a31b952341a534fe24890f1ed2921ee259773cff46e4f6273b8c4d5e3a", "e8ee6f5145c9d503c5130bfc6585567f6e19d409158c3c0ca0b259f1875b1a2f", "3e3901519c2305fbe9d5483b7234c25c6d2b562512916481d96f26b849c7d4e1", "9c2ce925133a3bf5a924063bbef8df49918d5b7258695c1894cd18c75970157a", "402625ec79e3573a80b6de9b33fc1e503e3c7803603cd958ddd515fb0e4a3c91", "b6cab0b3aa8e56e2427f486c74588d598ae58bb0cbc0eda6939fe171cb4f2d89", "d4e863f9818bfb2f1dd932df6441dff204e6142c3bdb55b298cb08dc7b6a9f12", "c6ef82d2864dfd26f117a1ef5602679153423f2742970a7949cec72722f0a0b3", "2a10ffe0367bb1b26ba2c3bc600892c21074725c0b8c9dc9161e6ceb339f4d5c"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: File or Process Matching Article Hash IOCs

status: experimental
description: |

    values. Use a watchlist or external indicator file for management
    at scale.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1027

    category: process_creation
    product: windows

    selection:
        Hashes|contains:
            - 'SHA256=__HASH_PLACEHOLDER_REPLACE_ME__'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - None on a true-positive hash match
level: critical

[LLM] Nx Console v18.95.0 payload — kitty/cat.py backdoor file drop Installation High
Detects creation of the Python C2 backdoor (cat.py) and its persistence artifacts at the specific kitty path used by the compromised Nx Console v18.95.0 extension (CVE-2026-48027). Article-specific paths apply to macOS, Linux and Windows variants of the dropper. Rationale: Anchored on the exact filenames and parent directories listed in the article IOC table (cat.py under kitty/, kitty-monitor.plist LaunchAgent, .gh_update_state anti-replay state file, /tmp/kitty-* staging). Cross-checked with CISA alert and the nrwl/nx-console GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w advisory. Cross-checked against: • https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2026/05/28/supply-chain-compromises-impact-nx-console-and-github-repositories • https://github.com/nrwl/nx-console/security/advisories/GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/compromised-nx-console-18950-targeted.html
ATT&CKT1195.001 T1059.006 T1543.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (FolderPath has @"\.local\share\kitty" and FileName =~ "cat.py")
     or (FolderPath has "/.local/share/kitty" and FileName =~ "cat.py")
     or (FolderPath has "/Library/LaunchAgents" and FileName =~ "com.user.kitty-monitor.plist")
     or (FolderPath startswith "/tmp/kitty-")
     or (FolderPath has "/var/tmp" and FileName =~ ".gh_update_state")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where (TargetFilePath has "kitty" and TargetFileName =~ "cat.py")
     or (TargetFilePath has "/LaunchAgents/" and TargetFileName =~ "com.user.kitty-monitor.plist")
     or TargetFilePath startswith "/tmp/kitty-"
     or (TargetFilePath has "/var/tmp" and TargetFileName =~ ".gh_update_state")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName,
          ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Nx Console Malicious Payload kitty/cat.py Backdoor File Drop
id: a4f6d2c8-91b3-4e7f-8c5a-1d9b7e3a6f02
description: Detects file creation of the Python C2 backdoor (cat.py) and its persistence artifacts at the kitty path used by the compromised Nx Console v18.95.0 extension (CVE-2026-48027).
references:
  - https://cybersecuritynews.com/attackers-abuse-trusted-developer-tooling/
  - https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2026/05/28/supply-chain-compromises-impact-nx-console-and-github-repositories

date: 2026/05/29

logsource:
  category: file_event
detection:
  selection_kitty_cat:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\.local\share\kitty\cat.py'
      - '/.local/share/kitty/cat.py'
  selection_plist:
    TargetFilename|contains: '/Library/LaunchAgents/com.user.kitty-monitor.plist'
  selection_anti_replay:

#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| TargetFileName=/(\\\\\.local\\\\share\\\\kitty\\\\cat\.py|\/\.local\/share\/kitty\/cat\.py|\/Library\/LaunchAgents\/com\.user\.kitty-monitor\.plist|\/tmp\/kitty-|\/var\/tmp\/\.gh_update_state)/i

[LLM] GitHub Search API dead-drop C2 polling (firedalazer marker) Command & Control High
Detects the Nx Console Python backdoor polling GitHub's commits-search API using the operator-specific marker token 'firedalazer' to receive signed remote commands. The marker is unique to this campaign and unlikely to appear in benign traffic. Rationale: The string 'firedalazer' is a campaign-unique search marker the backdoor embeds in the GitHub commits-search API query (api.github.com/search/commits?q=firedalazer). It has no benign meaning, so a single hit is high-fidelity. Cross-checked with StepSecurity write-up and CISA bulletin. Cross-checked against: • https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2026/05/28/supply-chain-compromises-impact-nx-console-and-github-repositories • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised • https://corgea.com/research/nx-console-vscode-extension-credential-stealer-may-2026
ATT&CKT1102.002 T1071.001 T1568
Data sourcesWeb.Web Network_Resolution.DNS Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
// Process-attributed network shape — the dead-drop poll always carries q=firedalazer
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has "api.github.com"
| where RemoteUrl has "firedalazer"
   or AdditionalFields has "firedalazer"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where HttpHostName has "api.github.com"
| where Url has "search/commits" and Url has "firedalazer"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, Url,
          HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, HttpMethod, DstHostname
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Megalodon C2 IP egress — 216.126.225.129:8443 Command & Control High
Detects outbound TCP connections to the Megalodon credential exfiltration C2 server (216.126.225.129:8443). Every connection from a corporate device to this IP+port pair is high-fidelity given the IP has no legitimate use. Rationale: 216.126.225.129:8443 is published in CISA's advisory and the article IOC table as the Megalodon C2 for credential exfiltration. Single-IOC IP/port match — no legitimate corporate traffic should reach this destination. Cross-checked with CISA advisory. Cross-checked against: • https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2026/05/28/supply-chain-compromises-impact-nx-console-and-github-repositories • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised • https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/github-breach-nx-console-vs-code/
ATT&CKT1041 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP == "216.126.225.129"
| where RemotePort == 8443 or RemotePort == 443
| summarize FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp),
            ConnectionCount = count(),
            BytesSentTotal = sum(tolong(extract(@"BytesSent.{0,3}(\d+)", 1, AdditionalFields)))
            by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
               InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by FirstSeen desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DstIpAddr == "216.126.225.129"
| where DstPortNumber in (8443, 443)
| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated),
            ConnectionCount = count(), TotalBytes = sum(NetworkBytes)
            by DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber,
               EventProduct
| order by FirstSeen desc

[LLM] AWS IMDS access from VS Code / Node / Bun developer tooling Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects access to the AWS instance-metadata service (169.254.169.254) or ECS task-role endpoint (169.254.170.2) initiated by developer tooling (VS Code, node, bun, python launched from a code workspace). The Nx Console payload uses this exact path to harvest AWS credentials on infected developer workstations and CI runners. Rationale: Article explicitly lists 169.254.169.254 (AWS IMDS) and 169.254.170.2 (ECS task-role) as targets of the credential-harvest module. Pairing the well-known credential-theft endpoint with developer-tooling parent processes filters out legitimate cloud-SDK use in EC2 workloads. Cross-checked with CISA advisory and StepSecurity write-up. Cross-checked against: • https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2026/05/28/supply-chain-compromises-impact-nx-console-and-github-repositories • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised • https://corgea.com/research/nx-console-vscode-extension-credential-stealer-may-2026
ATT&CKT1552.005 T1078.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Endpoint.Processes
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("169.254.169.254", "169.254.170.2")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("code", "node", "bun", "python", "python3", "electron")
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName has_any ("code", "Code Helper", "node", "bun")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in ("169.254.169.254", "169.254.170.2")
| join kind=inner (
    ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ActingProcessName has_any ("code", "node", "bun", "python", "python3", "electron")
       or ParentProcessName has_any ("code", "Code Helper", "node", "bun")
    | project DvcHostname, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessId, ParentProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
) on DvcHostname
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr,
          ActingProcessName, ParentProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] macOS LaunchAgent kitty-monitor persistence Installation High
Detects creation or modification of the com.user.kitty-monitor.plist LaunchAgent at ~/Library/LaunchAgents/ — the exact persistence mechanism the Nx Console Python backdoor installs on macOS to survive reboots. Rationale: The plist filename com.user.kitty-monitor.plist combined with the ~/Library/LaunchAgents/ path is unique to this campaign per the article IOC table. No legitimate macOS application uses this naming. Verified against CISA bulletin and the nrwl/nx-console GHSA advisory. Cross-checked against: • https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2026/05/28/supply-chain-compromises-impact-nx-console-and-github-repositories • https://github.com/nrwl/nx-console/security/advisories/GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/compromised-nx-console-18950-targeted.html
ATT&CKT1543.001 T1547
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FolderPath has "/Library/LaunchAgents"
| where FileName =~ "com.user.kitty-monitor.plist"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFilePath has "/Library/LaunchAgents"
| where TargetFileName =~ "com.user.kitty-monitor.plist"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName,
          ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Megalodon malicious GitHub Actions workflow file written to repo Delivery Medium
Detects checkout/clone of a Megalodon-tainted repository: a SysDiag.yml or Optimize-Build.yml file appearing under .github/workflows/. The Megalodon campaign mass-injected these specifically-named workflows into 5,561 repositories on 2026-05-18; the names are not used by any well-known CI template. Rationale: SysDiag and Optimize-Build are the article's named Megalodon workflow filenames (mass + targeted variants). The combination of .github/workflows/ path and exact filename is article-specific and would only appear on a host that cloned/pulled a tainted repo. Cross-checked with CISA advisory which urges audit of workflow files for commits after 2026-05-18. Cross-checked against: • https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2026/05/28/supply-chain-compromises-impact-nx-console-and-github-repositories • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised • https://www.ox.security/blog/teampcp-strikes-again-how-a-trojan-vs-code-extension-brought-down-github/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1098.004 T1554
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FolderPath has ".github" and FolderPath has "workflows"
| where FileName in~ ("SysDiag.yml", "SysDiag.yaml", "Optimize-Build.yml", "Optimize-Build.yaml")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFilePath has ".github" and TargetFilePath has "workflows"
| where TargetFileName in~ ("SysDiag.yml", "SysDiag.yaml", "Optimize-Build.yml", "Optimize-Build.yaml")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName,
          ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Megalodon Malicious GitHub Actions Workflow File
id: 6a3f817b-90a4-4d72-bd58-c50e6f4c8910
description: Detects file creation of SysDiag.yml or Optimize-Build.yml under .github/workflows/ — the campaign-specific filenames the Megalodon supply-chain attack injected into 5561 GitHub repositories on 2026-05-18.
references:
  - https://cybersecuritynews.com/attackers-abuse-trusted-developer-tooling/
  - https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2026/05/28/supply-chain-compromises-impact-nx-console-and-github-repositories
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/29

  - attack.t1554
logsource:
  category: file_event
detection:

source:(github.audit OR windows.sysmon OR linux.auditd) ((@TargetFilename:(*/.github/workflows/SysDiag.yml OR *\\.github\\workflows\\SysDiag.yml OR */.github/workflows/Optimize-Build.yml OR *\\.github\\workflows\\Optimize-Build.yml) OR @file.path:(*/.github/workflows/SysDiag.y* OR *.github*workflows*Optimize-Build.y*)) OR (@evt.name:(git.push OR workflow_run) AND @workflow.name:(SysDiag OR Optimize-Build)))
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| TargetFileName=/(\\\\|\/)\.github(\\\\|\/)workflows(\\\\|\/)(SysDiag|Optimize-Build)\.ya?ml$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName, UserName], function=count())

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-48027")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-48027")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9") or SHA1 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9") or MD5 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9") or SHA1 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9") or MD5 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Marimo CVE-2026-39987 /terminal/ws RCE: notebook process spawns shell or network tooling Exploitation High
Hunts the initial-access foothold described by Sysdig: an internet-reachable marimo notebook process (Python/uvicorn) spawns sh/bash/curl/wget/nc as a child of the unauthenticated /terminal/ws WebSocket exploit path. The marimo runtime should not be spawning shells or network egress utilities under normal load. Rationale: Anchors on the exact CVE-2026-39987 exploitation chain — marimo Python process spawning a shell/network utility through the unauthenticated /terminal/ws WebSocket. The parent-process predicate (marimo in cmdline of a Python/uvicorn parent) is the article-specific narrowing that distinguishes this from generic Python shellouts. Cross-checked with Sysdig blog and NVD entry confirming /terminal/ws is the exploit primitive. Cross-checked against: • https://webflow.sysdig.com/blog/ai-agent-at-the-wheel-how-an-attacker-used-llms-to-move-from-a-cve-to-an-internal-database-in-4-pivots • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-39987 • https://github.com/Nxploited/CVE-2026-39987
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("python","python3","uvicorn","gunicorn","marimo")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "marimo"
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","curl","wget","ncat","nc","busybox")
    or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/bin/sh","bash -c","/dev/tcp/","import socket","import pty")
| where not(FileName in~ ("python","python3") and ProcessCommandLine has "marimo")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("python","python3","uvicorn","gunicorn","marimo")
| where ParentProcessCommandLine has "marimo"
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("sh","bash","dash","curl","wget","ncat","nc","busybox")
    or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("/bin/sh","bash -c","/dev/tcp/","import socket","import pty")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, Hash
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Marimo Notebook Server Spawns Shell or Network Utility (CVE-2026-39987)
id: 7f3c2a91-9b5e-4d8a-b6c4-1e7f3a9d2c8e
status: experimental
description: Detects post-exploitation child processes spawned from a marimo notebook process — the fingerprint of CVE-2026-39987 abuse of the unauthenticated /terminal/ws endpoint.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/attackers-use-llm-agent-for-post.html
  - https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-39987
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/29
tags:
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.initial_access
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  parent_marimo:
    ParentImage|contains:
      - 'python'
      - 'uvicorn'
      - 'gunicorn'
    ParentCommandLine|contains: 'marimo'
  child_shell:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/sh'
      - '/bash'
      - '/dash'
      - '/curl'
      - '/wget'
      - '/ncat'
      - '/nc'
  child_cmd_markers:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '/dev/tcp/'
      - 'bash -c'
      - 'import socket'
      - 'import pty'
  condition: parent_marimo and (child_shell or child_cmd_markers)
falsepositives:
  - Notebook author legitimately running shell commands inside the marimo kernel (treat as anomaly worth review)
level: high
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE (@process.parent.name:(python OR python3 OR uvicorn OR gunicorn) AND @process.parent.command_line:*marimo*) AND (@process.executable.path:(*/bin/sh OR */bin/bash OR */bin/dash OR */usr/bin/curl OR */usr/bin/wget OR */usr/bin/nc OR */usr/bin/ncat) OR @process.command_line:(*"/dev/tcp/"* OR *"bash -c"* OR *"import socket"*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^(python|python3|python3\.[0-9]+|uvicorn|gunicorn)$/i
| ParentCommandLine=/marimo/i
| (ImageFileName=/\/(sh|bash|dash|curl|wget|nc|ncat|busybox)$/i OR CommandLine=/(\/dev\/tcp\/|bash -c|import socket|import pty)/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentCommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT

[LLM] AWS Secrets Manager GetSecretValue fan-out from multiple egress IPs Actions on Objectives High
Detects the LLM-agent fingerprint of replaying a single stolen IAM credential through a fanned-out egress pool: the same principal/access key calls GetSecretValue on the same secret from 3+ distinct source IPs in a short window — the IP diversification pattern Sysdig saw used to retrieve the SSH private key. Rationale: Targets the article's defining cloud-credential abuse signature: 'replayed them through a fanned-out egress pool to retrieve an SSH private key from AWS Secrets Manager.' The fan-out is the high-fidelity anomaly — legitimate apps call Secrets Manager from a stable set of IPs (NAT gateway, Lambda, EKS pod IP). The Datadog version also pins the five Cloudflare-egress IPs Sysdig observed. Sentinel/Defender empty: schema reference doesn't include AWSCloudTrail and Defender Advanced Hunting doesn't ingest CloudTrail. [LLM] SSH private key file enumeration then read (ls id_ed25519* → cat id_ed25519) Actions on Objectives High
Detects the LLM-agent value-handoff pattern Sysdig documented: an `ls -la ~/.ssh/id_ed25519*` existence check followed within seconds by `cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519` on the same host/user. The list-then-read sequence on the exact same path is a strong indicator of programmatic (agent) operation, not a human reading the file directly. Rationale: Anchors on the exact behavioural fingerprint Sysdig called out as agent-confirmation: 'a cat command to print the contents of a specific file (cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519) is preceded by an ls command that passes the same file pattern as input (ls -la ~/.ssh/id_ed25519*) to confirm that the SSH Key exists.' The list-then-read within 60s, same user/host, is the high-fidelity tell — humans rarely script this; agents check existence before consumption.
